members.duties: mechanics audit: damage-budget compliance (flat numbers on Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21), prereq shapes (Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3), cost math (cards 2/4/8), level gates, dice remnants, stale vocabulary, cross-chapter contradictions
consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance
final quality: structure, cross-references, missing content, completeness
presentation: Quarto/Typst render, heading hierarchy, table formatting/overflow, typography, page flow, card layout, reference-sheet usability, em-dash law

payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch20 (quarto-book/chapters/20-bestiary.qmd), "Bestiary", 322 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (20-bestiary.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06: Boon/Bane, difficulty ladder +2/+0/-2/-4; combat = ch13:
conditions and their leveled forms (Burning X, Slowed X, Poisoned X, Dazed
X, Frozen X), Surprised, resistance half/double, "no surprise rounds"
phraseology; classes = ch05: the nine classes and their names; skills =
ch07: the 23-skill roster (Deception IS on it, keyed Guile); magic = ch11/
ch12: spell names (Turn Unholy is the spell; the Shepherd's class signature
is Turn Undead and still exists in ch05); advancement = ch18: follower
counts/1d3 precedent, stronghold HP; GM guidance = ch19: encounter
multiplier semantics (a creature's Challenge is its share of the budget),
faction actions; glossary = ch21; reference tables = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, band values,
                  vocabulary swaps, stat-block arithmetic)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; monster stat
blocks CONFORM to challenge bands (C1-2 -> 2/4/6, C3-6 -> 6/9/12, C7+ ->
9/15/21), secondary attacks at most one tier lower than the primary; card
costs 2/4/8 DP; no flat +N damage riders anywhere in the book (a damage
bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of 1/2/3 + attribute, or a
"+1 damage tier" bump); one-roll principle; damage dice are dead outside the
allowed random-table exceptions (1d4/1d6 random behavior, 1d4+1 duration
dice); ZERO "save" vocabulary (resistance = attribute CHECKS: "Fortitude
check", "Guile check"); leveled conditions carry a number (Slowed X, Poisoned
X), bespoke phrasings like "speed halved" or "dazed for 1 round" are stale
vocabulary; attribute ceiling -2 to +2; class names are exactly the nine
from ch05; monster HP is a GUIDELINE ("HP ~= 5 x Challenge, adjust to
taste") and printed HP values are NOT findings. Violations of these
conventions are findings, not questions.

Scope note: this chapter is the canonical home for stat blocks, monster
creation, and encounter building. Where another chapter contradicts it, the
finding should name BOTH files and identify which is canonical. The council's
output is a disposition plan; it does not itself edit the book.

payload.argument: ch20 cannot ship as written: it still carries the defect classes the 2026-08-19 rulings were meant to remove, plus fresh convention breaks. The Fire Elemental (20-bestiary.qmd:174) keeps a 'Vulnerable: Water' entry that deals a flat 2 cold damage when splashed, where the half/double law requires doubled damage of a real type; Water is not among the 13 damage types, and the expected form is a doubled-damage vulnerability to a real type such as Cold. The Shadow Stalker (20-bestiary.qmd:238) labels its bright-light weakness 'Vulnerable: Light', granting Boon on attacks against it and cutting its own damage tier, which doubles nothing; Light is not a damage type, so this is a bespoke ability mislabeled with the vulnerability keyword, expected to be renamed (or converted to doubled Radiant). The Phase Beast's death burst (20-bestiary.qmd:264) resolves with an 'Agility save for half', the banned save word; expected an Agility check for half. The Water Elemental (20-bestiary.qmd:176) still phrases its freeze as 'speed halved for 1 round', and the Pixie (20-bestiary.qmd:154) makes a target 'roll Weak on its next action'; both are bespoke phrasings where ch13's leveled conditions (Slowed X, Confused X) are the canonical forms. Five stat blocks grant flat off-budget damage values: the Fire Elemental touch aura (2 fire), the Barbed Devil hide (2 piercing), the Dryad treebound drain (3 per round), the Swarm of Rats automatic 1, and the Stirge drain while attached (2 per round); the book only permits budget-row or tier-bump expressions. The Encounter Building examples (20-bestiary.qmd:288-290) also total 2, 4, and 8 budget points for a level-3 party while the Easy/Standard/Hard multipliers call for 3, 6, and 9. Every item is a mechanical vocabulary or arithmetic swap; no HP, band, or attack values change.

evidence.claim: The Phase Beast's Unstable detonation (20-bestiary.qmd:264) resolves with an Agility save for half damage, which is the banned save vocabulary; the book requires attribute checks, so this must read as an Agility check for half.

The Fire Elemental (20-bestiary.qmd:174) is printed as Vulnerable to Water with a flat 2 cold damage splash effect. Water is not one of the 13 damage types and the effect is not doubled damage, so the entry breaks the half/double vulnerability law; expected a real type with doubled damage, e.g. Vulnerable: Cold (takes double cold damage).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: takes 2 cold damage when splashed with water

evidence.claim: The Shadow Stalker (20-bestiary.qmd:238) applies the Vulnerability keyword to a bright-light weakness that grants Boon on attacks against it and reduces its own damage tier, doubling nothing; since Light is not a damage type, this should be a separate light-sensitivity ability rather than a Vulnerability.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: all attacks against the stalker are at Boon

evidence.claim: The Water Elemental's Freeze (20-bestiary.qmd:176) still uses the stale 'speed halved' phrasing where ch13's leveled Slowed X condition (speed reduced by X feet) is canonical, e.g. Slowed 15 for a 30-ft speed creature, and the Pixie's Confusion Touch (20-bestiary.qmd:154) makes a target 'roll Weak' instead of applying the ch13 Confused X condition.

Five stat blocks grant flat off-budget damage: the Swarm of Rats (20-bestiary.qmd:70) deals automatic 1 damage, the Stirge (20-bestiary.qmd:76) drains 2 per round while attached, the Dryad (20-bestiary.qmd:156) takes 3 per round away from its tree, the Fire Elemental (20-bestiary.qmd:174) deals 2 fire on touch, and the Barbed Devil (20-bestiary.qmd:194) deals 2 piercing on contact; none is a budget-row or tier-bump expression, violating the zero-rider law.

The Encounter Building example rows (20-bestiary.qmd:288-290) for a level-3 party total 2, 4, and 8 budget points against the Easy/Standard/Hard multipliers of 3, 6, and 9 (4 Wolves at C1/2 = 2; Knight + 2 Guards = 4; Young Dragon + 4 Cultists = 8), so the examples should be adjusted to sum to the stated budgets, e.g. 6 Wolves, 2 Knights, and a Young Dragon plus 6 Cultists.

payload.argument: The chapter does not hold under the standing conventions and cannot ship as written; the defects cluster in stat-block vocabulary, two off-band stat blocks, and encounter-table arithmetic. The clearest single breach is the Phase Beast's death burst at 20-bestiary.qmd:264, which demands an Agility save, the one word the book's resistance vocabulary bans (resistance is always an attribute check). The Archmage at line 92 is rated Challenge 6, yet its at-will Dagger and Ember Lance sit on the 2/4/6 row, a full band below the 6/9/12 the chapter's own creation rules (lines 304-307) lock for C3-6; only the once-per-encounter Brimstone Burst reaches the correct row, the same band defect the ch19 council flagged in Kelvath, inverted. The Barbed Devil's claw at line 194 bolts a flat +2 fire bonus onto a 6/9/12 row, and its Barbed Hide, the Fire Elemental's Touch, and its water vulnerability deal static 2s, none of which is a permitted damage form (budget row, basic-card floor, or +1 damage tier bump). Condition vocabulary drifts into bespoke phrasing: Water Elemental Freeze (line 176) halves speed for a round where the leveled form is Slowed with a number; the Ghoul (line 128) and Vrock (line 192) apply Paralyzed and Stunned for one round, while ch13's condition table ends both at source duration and gives its leveled conditions a number. Two abilities grant flat +1 check bonuses where the convention is Boon/Bane: the Bugbear's Natural Stealth (line 102) also mis-keys Stealth to Guile although ch07 keys it to Agility, and the Doppelganger's Deceptive (line 206) adds +1 to Guile (Deception) checks. The Lich's phylactery (line 132) reforms in 1d10 days, a die outside the allowed set of 1d4/1d6 random behavior and 1d4+1 duration dice. The Encounter Building examples (lines 288-291) do not sum to the stated budgets for a level-3 party under the chapter's own footnote that C½ equals Challenge ½: four Wolves total 2 against an Easy budget of 3, one Knight plus two Guards total 4 against a Standard budget of 6, and one Young Dragon plus four Cultists total 8 against a Hard budget of 9. Smaller items: the Zombie's Relentless (line 126) says to roll Fortitude instead of making a Fortitude check like every sibling block, and the Dryad's Treebound (line 156) deals a flat 3 matching no budget row. On the support side, the chapter holds the em-dash law (zero violations), names the nine classes correctly (Arcanist, Shepherd), and nearly every other stat block conforms to its band with proper attribute-check phrasing; those strengths do not offset the violations above.

evidence.claim: The Phase Beast's Unstable death burst uses 'save' vocabulary, which the book's resistance convention bans; resistance is expressed as attribute checks ('Fortitude check', 'Guile check'), so the line should read as an Agility check for half damage.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Unstable:** When the phase beast is reduced to 0 HP, it explodes. All creatures within 10 ft take 6/9/12 force damage (Agility save for half).

evidence.claim: The Archmage is Challenge 6, so its effective primary (the at-will attacks) must use the C3-6 row 6/9/12 per the chapter's own creation bands; its Dagger and Ember Lance sit a full band lower at 2/4/6, with only the once-per-encounter Brimstone Burst on the correct row.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Archmage (Challenge 6):** HP 14, DR 2. Dagger: 2/4/6. Ember Lance: 2/4/6 (at will). Brimstone Burst: 6/9/12 (once per encounter). Counterspell: reaction to negate a spell.

evidence.claim: The chapter's monster-creation rules lock the damage rows to challenge bands, stating C3-6 (Adept) as W:6 / S:9 / St:12, which is the reference the Archmage's 2/4/6 at-will attacks violate.
The Barbed Devil's claw bolts a flat '+2 fire' bonus onto a 6/9/12 budget row, a damage rider the book only permits as a budget row, a basic-card floor, or a '+1 damage tier' bump.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Barbed Devil (Challenge 5):** HP 22, DR 4. Claw: 6/9/12 + 2 fire. Tail: 6/9/12 piercing.

evidence.claim: Contact and vulnerability effects deal static damage amounts (2 fire, 2 cold, 2 piercing) that are not W/S/S rows and act as flat riders outside the attack model.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Touch: creatures touching or hitting the elemental take 2 fire. Vulnerable: Water (takes 2 cold damage when splashed with water).

evidence.claim: 'Speed halved for 1 round' is the bespoke phrasing the book's convention replaces with a leveled condition; the canonical form is Slowed with a number (Slowed X), which ch13 defines as a speed reduction in feet.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Freeze: when hit by cold damage, speed halved for 1 round.

evidence.claim: The Ghoul imposes Paralyzed with a fixed 'for 1 round' duration, but ch13's condition table ends Paralyzed at 'Source duration' and gives no 'for 1 round' form; the bespoke duration phrasing is stale vocabulary.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Paralyzing Touch: on Strong claw hit, target must make a Fortitude check or be Paralyzed for 1 round.

evidence.claim: The Vrock's Stunning Screech imposes Stunned 'for 1 round', repeating the bespoke fixed-duration phrasing; ch13's condition table ends Stunned at 'Source duration'.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Stunning Screech (1/day): all within 30 ft must make a Fortitude check or be Stunned for 1 round.

evidence.claim: The combat chapter's condition table ends both Paralyzed and Stunned at 'Source duration' and reserves numbered durations for its leveled conditions, confirming that 'for 1 round' is not the canonical phrasing for these conditions.
The Bugbear's Natural Stealth is a flat '+1' check rider where the convention is Boon/Bane, and it mis-keys the Stealth skill to Guile; the expected form is Boon on Agility (Stealth) checks.
The skills chapter keys Stealth to Agility, not Guile, so 'Guile (Stealth)' is a mis-keyed check.
The Doppelganger's Deceptive grants a flat '+1' to Guile (Deception) checks where the convention requires Boon/Bane phrasing; the skill key itself is correct per ch07 (Deception keys to Guile).
The Lich's phylactery reformation uses a 1d10 die, which is outside the book's allowed dice set (1d4/1d6 random behavior, 1d4+1 duration dice); expected a 1d4+1 or 1d6-based duration.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Phylactery: reforms in 1d10 days if phylactery survives.

evidence.claim: The encounter table's own footnote defines C½ as Challenge ½, the premise for the example arithmetic.

Under that definition, the three worked examples do not sum to the stated budgets for a level-3 party: four Wolves total 2 against an Easy budget of 3, one Knight plus two Guards total 4 against a Standard budget of 6, and one Young Dragon plus four Cultists total 8 against a Hard budget of 9.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt:
| Easy | × party level | 4 Wolves (C½ each) |
| Standard | ×2 party level | 1 Knight (C3) + 2 Guards (C½ each) |
| Hard | ×3 party level | 1 Young Dragon (C6) + 4 Cultists (C½) |

evidence.claim: The Zombie's Relentless drops the word 'check', reading 'roll Fortitude', while the Dire Boar, Orc, and every other Relentless entry say 'make a Fortitude check'; the phrasing is inconsistent within the chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Relentless: when reduced to 0 HP, roll Fortitude. On Strong, stays at 1 HP.

evidence.claim: The Dryad's Treebound deals a flat 3 damage per round, a value on no budget row (2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21), repeating the off-budget flat-value pattern the ch19 audit flagged.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Treebound: takes 3 damage per round when more than 300 ft from its bonded tree.

payload.argument: The chapter cannot ship as the canonical home for stat blocks and monster creation: its design-authority section and its own stat blocks contradict each other and the locked conventions. [264] The only resistance roll in the chapter is written as an 'Agility save', exactly the vocabulary the standing convention bans in favor of attribute checks. [176] The Water Elemental's Freeze uses 'speed halved for 1 round', the stale phrasing the conventions replaced with the numbered leveled condition, while the same chapter writes 'Poisoned 2' correctly at line 62, so the chapter is inconsistent with itself. [102,184,206] Two modifier systems run in parallel: Natural Stealth and Deceptive grant flat +1 to checks and Pack Tactics, Leadership, and Marshal Undead grant flat +1 to attacks, while Stone Camouflage, Magic Resistance, and the Shadow Stalker's light vulnerability express the same kinds of effects as Boon/Bane, so a GM cannot know which system is canonical when building monsters; the Bandit's Pack Tactics at line 84 is a dangling reference with no effect text. [297] The Creating Monsters rule sets DR by a formula that more than a dozen natural-armor stat blocks in the same chapter ignore (Dire Wolf C1 prints DR 1 against a formula value of 0, Green Hag C3 prints 2 against 1, Wyrmling C3 prints 3 against 1), and only HP carries the adjust-to-taste hedge, so the printed DRs are neither formula-conformant nor declared hand-tuned. [302] The Quick Monster Template limits Challenge to 1-12 yet the chapter prints Challenge 1/2 monsters throughout and its own encounter table defines that as the minion tier, so the template cannot produce the chapter's own creatures. [132] The Lich's phylactery roll uses 1d10 days, outside the book's allowed dice. Tested and clean: no em-dashes, all printed damage rows conform to their challenge bands, attributes stay within the ceiling, class names match ch05, Morale Check is a defined mechanic (13:257), and Surprised uses ch13 vocabulary.

evidence.claim: Line 264 is the chapter's only resistance roll and it uses the banned 'save' vocabulary; the standing convention requires attribute checks, so this must read 'Agility check for half'.

Line 176 Freeze uses the stale 'speed halved' phrasing the conventions replaced with the numbered leveled condition Slowed X (defined at 13:187); the chapter itself uses the correct form 'Poisoned 2' at line 62.

Natural Stealth (line 102) and Deceptive (line 206) grant flat +1 to skill checks while Stone Camouflage (line 184) grants Boon on Stealth for the same kind of effect; the chapter's own Boon/Bane usage (lines 104, 186, 192, 194, 232, 238) makes the flat +1s drift from the core modifier system.

Pack Tactics (lines 38, 46), Leadership (line 90), and Marshal Undead (line 274) grant flat +1 to attacks or attack rolls while the same chapter expresses attack modifiers as Bane (line 104) and Boon (line 238); the Bandit's 'Pack Tactics.' at line 84 has no effect text at all.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +1 to attacks when an ally is adjacent.

evidence.claim: The Creating Monsters DR formula (line 297) is contradicted by the chapter's own natural-armor stat blocks: Dire Wolf (C1) prints DR 1 against formula 0, Green Hag (C3) prints 2 against 1, Wyrmling (C3) prints 3 against 1; only HP carries an 'adjust to taste' hedge, so the printed DRs are neither formula-conformant nor declared hand-tuned.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: DR = Challenge ÷ 2 (round down), based on natural armor (max 6)

evidence.claim: The Quick Monster Template restricts Challenge to 1-12 (line 302), which excludes the Challenge 1/2 monsters printed throughout the chapter (Wolf, Goblin, Bandit, Orc, Skeleton, Zombie, Pixie, and more) and the encounter table's own minion tier defined at line 284.

The Lich's phylactery roll (line 132) uses 1d10 days, outside the allowed dice (1d4/1d6 random behavior, 1d4+1 duration dice); the Death Knight's 1d4 rounds at line 278 is likewise a plain duration die outside the stated 1d4+1 form.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: reforms in 1d10 days if phylactery survives

payload.argument: Refute: ch20 does not hold on voice and consistency as written, though nothing here requires touching monster math. The Creating Monsters section (20-bestiary.qmd:295-308) states its own rules twice within nine lines and the copies disagree: the opening paragraph promises 1-3 attacks and 1-2 abilities, while the Quick Monster Template directly below caps attacks at 1-2 and abilities at a single signature entry, and the HP/DR formula appears twice with the natural-armor ceiling present only in the first copy. A GM building a monster therefore gets two conflicting construction rules from one section. The Additional Monsters section (20-bestiary.qmd:210-278) reads like a different editorial pass: it is the only place in the chapter that opens a stat block with an italic one-line tagline in a noticeably punchier register, while the other forty-plus entries are plain utility prose; the device must either be removed or applied uniformly, and the minimal edit is to remove it. Identically named abilities are worded differently between entries: Pack Tactics on the Wolf versus the Dire Wolf, Charge on the Dire Boar versus the Minotaur, and Relentless in three variants, one of which uses 'roll Fortitude' where the book standard is a Fortitude check. The same once-per-day frequency is written two ways, as the phrase and as the parenthetical shorthand. The Zombie's trait named Slow is a near-homonym of the combat chapter's Slowed X condition even though the two mechanics are unrelated, an avoidable name collision for a GM-facing book. Both illustration captions carry art-tracker residue (placeholder status and pixel dimensions) that must not reach print. Disposition: every item is a mechanical vocabulary or wording swap (canonicalize the monster-creation numbers, standardize each shared ability sentence, drop the taglines, rename the Zombie trait, strip the tracker text), with extending the tagline device to the whole chapter as the larger, conditional alternative.

evidence.claim: The Creating Monsters opening (20-bestiary.qmd:297) directs the GM to give 1-3 attacks and add 1-2 abilities, while the Quick Monster Template a few lines below (20-bestiary.qmd:304, 308) caps attacks at 1-2 and abilities at a single signature ability, so the section offers two conflicting monster-construction rules.

The monster HP and DR formula is printed twice in the same section (20-bestiary.qmd:297 and 20-bestiary.qmd:303) and the two copies diverge: only the first carries the natural-armor ceiling of 6, so the repeated statement of the rule is not identical.

The Additional Monsters entries (Cave Troll through Death Knight, 20-bestiary.qmd:212-278) each open with a one-line italic tagline in a markedly punchier register, a device used by none of the other roughly forty stat blocks in the chapter; the section therefore reads as a different editorial treatment of the same content.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You won't see it coming. You'll feel it leave.

evidence.claim: The identically named Pack Tactics ability is phrased differently on the Wolf (20-bestiary.qmd:38) and the Dire Wolf (20-bestiary.qmd:46), and the identically named Charge ability differs between the Dire Boar (20-bestiary.qmd:78) and the Minotaur (20-bestiary.qmd:146); shared abilities should share one canonical sentence.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +1 to attacks when an ally is adjacent

evidence.claim: Relentless appears in three wordings across the Dire Boar (20-bestiary.qmd:78), the Orc (20-bestiary.qmd:110), and the Zombie (20-bestiary.qmd:126), the Zombie variant using the nonstandard 'roll Fortitude' where the book standard is a Fortitude check.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: roll Fortitude. On Strong, stays at 1 HP

evidence.claim: The once-per-day frequency is written as a phrase on the Orc (20-bestiary.qmd:110) and the Pixie (20-bestiary.qmd:154) but as parenthetical shorthand on the Lich, Dryad, Green Hag, and Vrock (20-bestiary.qmd:132, 156, 158, 192).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: once per day, when reduced to 0 HP

evidence.claim: The Zombie trait Slow (20-bestiary.qmd:126), which makes the creature act last in initiative, is a near-homonym of the combat chapter's leveled Slowed X condition (13-combat.qmd:187), which reduces speed; two unrelated mechanics share a near-identical name, inviting misreading.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Slow: always acts last in initiative

evidence.claim: Both chapter-art captions (20-bestiary.qmd:9 and 20-bestiary.qmd:118) carry art-tracker residue in the form of placeholder status and pixel dimensions, which is out of book voice and would ship in print if left in place.

payload.argument: The chapter cannot ship as the canonical stat-block reference: its own grammar section and the rest of the book never define the keywords its stat blocks lean on hardest. Recharge rides on thirteen abilities here and appears in a different, die-based form in the ch19 Kelvath block, yet no chapter defines the keyword and the Reading a Stat Block field table does not explain any frequency vocabulary (Recharge, at will, once per encounter, N/day), so a GM running these monsters cannot learn how often a gated power returns; that is a rule referenced but never defined, in the one chapter that must define it. The chapter is also structured two ways at once: ten monsters in the Beasts and Additional Monsters sections carry third-level headings while the remaining three dozen-plus entries in the other twelve sections are bold run-ins, and the Beasts section even mixes both formats within itself, so the generated navigation surfaces only a fraction of the roster. The Bear's Multiattack borrows 'Standard Action', a term no chapter defines; the combat chapter's economy speaks of Action, Maneuver, and Movement, and every other action reference in this chapter says 'as an action'. Finally, the Encounter Building section is a footnote and a table with no rule text connecting party level, the multiplier, and the sum of creature Challenges, so a reader who lands there has to reverse-engineer the procedure. The load-bearing gap is Recharge: stat-block grammar without a definition, and the book's only stat-block chapter is exactly where it must be supplied.

evidence.claim: Thirteen stat-block abilities in this chapter carry the Recharge keyword (Web, Hex, War Cry, Fire Breath, the three dragon Breath Weapons, Spores, Mind Reading, Shadow Leap, Rooted Grasp, Blink, Hellfire Orb) and none of them or any other passage says when the ability becomes usable again; the Reading a Stat Block table's six fields (Name, Attributes, HP, DR, Attacks, Abilities) cover no frequency keyword at all.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Web (Recharge):** Ranged attack that Restrains target on hit.

evidence.claim: The one other stat block in the book writes the same keyword with a recovery range: Tidal Surge is gated 'Recharge 5-6', which implies a die roll that the bare Recharge form never states; the two stat-block chapters disagree on what the keyword means, and this chapter is the canonical home for stat blocks.

Exactly ten monsters in two sections use third-level headings (five in Beasts, five in Additional Monsters) while every other monster, more than three dozen entries across twelve sections, is a bold run-in, so the book's generated navigation lists only the ten headed entries and a reader cannot jump to the Lich, the Doppelganger, or the Gelatinous Cube from the contents.

The split is visible inside a single section: the Beasts section heads its first five entries (Wolf through Swarm of Rats) as third-level headings and then prints Stirge and Dire Boar as bold run-ins immediately after, so the heading level does not track any content distinction.

The Bear's Multiattack is the only action reference in the book that says 'Standard Action'; every other action reference in this chapter says 'as an action' or names a Maneuver, and the combat chapter's economy never uses the term, so it is vocabulary with no definition anywhere in the rulebook.

The combat chapter defines the turn economy as Action, Movement, and Maneuver, and its tables label basic maneuvers like Disengage, confirming that 'Standard Action' is not part of the game's action vocabulary.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Move 5 ft without provoking opportunity attacks

evidence.claim: The frequency grammar is split three ways inside the chapter: at will, once per encounter (Brimstone Burst), and per-day counts (Disrupt Life, Charm, Stunning Screech, Legendary Resistance), none of which the Reading a Stat Block section explains.

The Encounter Building section consists of a footnote defining C½ and a four-row table; no sentence states that the budget equals the party level times the multiplier or that creature Challenges are summed to fill it, so the procedure a DA needs to build an encounter is missing from the section that exists for that purpose.

payload.argument: The chapter does not render as one uniform reference grammar: only ten stat blocks are set as headed blocks with one ability per line, while the remaining thirty-plus blocks are inline bold paragraph walls, and both grammars sit side by side inside the Beasts section. On the built page the paragraph-wall entries become wrapped four-to-six-line runs whose ability names surface mid-paragraph, so a GM cannot scan to an ability, which breaks the chapter's own stat-block-readability promise and the reference-sheet usability bar. Typography also drifts inside Creating Monsters, where numeric ranges mix plain hyphens with en-dashes against the book's en-dash range convention, and forced page breaks strand sparse content on otherwise blank pages. All fixes are mechanical: promote every stat block to the headed line-per-ability form, unify range dashes, and reflow the near-empty pages.

evidence.claim: The Beasts section opens with five stat blocks set as third-level headings, then switches to inline bold paragraph leads for Stirge and Dire Boar, so a single section renders two different stat-block grammars.

On the built page the bold-lead entries render as wrapped four-to-six-line paragraphs with no heading ornament and no line break between abilities, while headed entries get a distinct glyph; the Doppelganger's Ambusher and Deceptive land at the tail of a six-line run, unreachable by scanning.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Ambusher: +1 damage tier against surprised targets.

evidence.claim: The Quick Monster Template uses hyphenated ranges for attack and ability counts and for the Challenge bound, while the challenge-band rows immediately below use en-dashes; ch13 and ch19 use en-dashes for ranges, so the section is internally split and drifts from book convention.
The band rows directly under the template steps express the same kind of numeric span with en-dashes, proving the hyphen/en-dash split is within one section.

Forced page breaks strand sparse content on near-empty pages: the three-line intro paragraph alone on p.319, Dire Boar alone on p.322, and the single-monster Oozes and Shapechangers sections alone on pp.334-335, each page mostly whitespace.
The chapter promises stat blocks read like character sheets, i.e. one uniform grammar; the paragraph-wall blocks contradict that promise on the page.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: If you can read a character sheet, you can read a stat block.

payload.argument: On balance the chapter cannot ship as a single publishable unit: most of the filed defects check out against the text and the authoritative chapters, and the work ahead is broad but shallow. Confirmed against the source: the lone resistance roll worded as a save, the halved-speed freeze phrasing, the flat damage riders, the mis-totalled encounter examples, the never-defined recharge keyword, the split stat-block grammar, the duplicated and conflicting monster-creation guidance, the challenge template that cannot make minions, the d10 phylactery roll, and the art-tracker captions. Three claims do not hold: the archmage's at-will rows are a permitted one-tier-lower secondary pattern, the one-round paralyzed and stunned durations are compliant source durations, and the fire elemental's water vulnerability is a self-defining bespoke trait rather than a broken keyword. The confirmed set is almost entirely mechanical vocabulary and arithmetic swaps; a small group of items (flat check modifiers versus boon and bane, hazard damage expression, the damage-reduction formula versus printed monsters, and the pixie effect) needs a design ruling with a recommended default, and nothing in this round demands a multi-file implementation pass.

evidence.claim: The only resistance roll in the chapter is worded as an agility save for half, which clashes with the bookwide rule that resistance always takes the form of an attribute check; the expected wording is an agility check for half.

The water elemental's freeze effect still uses the old halved-speed phrasing that the leveled slowed condition with a number replaced; the canonical expression keys the reduction to feet rather than halves.

The fire elemental's water vulnerability is self-defining: it states its own flat cold damage on splashing rather than pretending to be a standard doubled-damage vulnerability, so it reads as a bespoke trait, not a broken keyword use, and the claims filed against it are false positives.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: takes 2 cold damage when splashed with water

evidence.claim: The ghoul and vrock conditions with a fixed one-round duration are legitimate: the combat chapter ends both conditions at source duration, meaning the applying ability sets how long they last, so a stated one-round span is the source duration rather than stale vocabulary, and the claims against them are false positives.

The archmage's at-will attacks sit one tier below its strongest strike, which the book permits for secondary attacks, so the claimed band violation is a false positive; its damage rows are all inside the allowed band system.

Several entries deal flat damage amounts outside the attack model, and the barbed devil's claw adds a flat two fire on top of a full row; the book only allows damage expressed through budget rows, basic-card floors, or a tier bump, so these must be converted.

The three worked encounter examples for a level-three party total two, four, and eight budget points while the easy, standard, and hard multipliers for that party are three, six, and nine, so the examples undercount by one party-level share each.

The recharge keyword appears on more than a dozen abilities yet no passage in the book defines when it resets, and the only other stat block in the book writes it with a recovery range; the reading-a-stat-block table covers no frequency vocabulary, leaving a real grammar gap.
Ten monsters use third-level headings while the remaining three dozen-plus entries are bold paragraph leads, and one section mixes both forms, so the navigation and scan affordance are inconsistent.

The monster-creation section repeats its own guidance and the copies conflict: the opening allows one to three attacks and one to two abilities while the template caps attacks at two and abilities at one, and the damage-reduction formula appears twice with the ceiling only in the first copy.
The quick template's challenge range starts at one, which cannot produce the half-challenge minions the chapter itself prints and that its own encounter table defines as a tier.

The creation formula for damage reduction conflicts with printed natural-armor monsters in the same chapter, and unlike hit points, damage reduction carries no hand-tuning hedge, so the mismatch is unexplained.
The lich's phylactery timer uses a d10, a die outside the book's permitted set for random behavior and durations; the expected form is the d4-plus-one style used elsewhere.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: reforms in 1d10 days if phylactery survives

evidence.claim: The bear's multiattack is the only place in the book using the standard-action term, which no chapter defines; the rest of the book says as an action.

The five additional monsters open with italic taglines in a punchier register that none of the other forty or so entries use, so the section reads as a different editorial treatment; the minimal fix is removing them.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You won't see it coming. You'll feel it leave.

evidence.claim: A bugbear trait keys the stealth skill to guile, but the skills chapter keys stealth to agility, a plain cross-chapter mismatch, and the same trait plus a doppelganger trait grant flat plus-one check bonuses where the book expresses modifiers as boon or bane.
Art-tracker residue with placeholder status and pixel dimensions sits in both illustration captions and must not reach print.

The shadow stalker's light weakness is a real but low-severity keyword mislabel: it grants boon and cuts a damage tier rather than doubling damage, so it should be renamed as a bespoke sensitivity; the pixie's weak-roll effect is not an exact match for the combat chapter's confused condition, so converting it is a mechanical change rather than a straight vocabulary swap.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: all attacks against the stalker are at Boon

payload.rationale: t-01 rejected 7-0 in round 1 (7 refute, 0 support, un_rebutted f-001..f-007). The librarian's synthesis confirmed the large mechanical set (save vocabulary, leveled-condition phrasing, flat riders, encounter sums, undefined Recharge, split stat-block grammar, duplicated-conflicting creation rules, C1/2 template gap, 1d10, Standard Action, taglines, skill-key mismatch, art captions) and dismissed three false positives with reasons: the Archmage's at-will rows are a permitted one-tier-lower secondary pattern, the Paralyzed/Stunned one-round durations are compliant source durations, and the Fire Elemental water vulnerability is a self-defining bespoke trait. The stat-block grammar fork (promote vs demote) resolves to PROMOTE on the layout-expert's built-PDF evidence: paragraph-wall entries render as wrapped four-to-six-line runs whose ability names surface mid-paragraph, breaking the chapter's own 'read it like a character sheet' promise and reference-sheet usability; demoting would apply that defect to the whole roster. The +1-modifier conversion follows the ch17 #384 precedent (flat +N -> Boon/Bane). The DR formula mismatch gets the same hand-tuning hedge the chapter already gives HP. Confidence 0.9.
payload.recommendation: REJECTED 7-0: ch20 is not publishable as-is. Ship the disposition as ONE atomic ch20 PR (no other chapter needs touching). MECHANICAL (micro-PR): (1) Phase Beast 264 'Agility save for half' -> 'Agility check for half' (save ban); (2) Water Elemental 176 'speed halved for 1 round' -> 'Slowed 10 for 1 round' (leveled-condition vocabulary); (3) Barbed Devil 194 'Claw: 6/9/12 + 2 fire' -> 'Claw: 6/9/12 slashing' (zero-rider law; the flat +2 makes 8/11/14, not rows); (4) encounter examples 288-291 re-totalled to the ×-multiplier budgets (Easy x1=3: 6 Wolves C½; Standard x2=6: 1 Knight C3 + 6 Guards C½; Hard x3=9: 1 Young Dragon C6 + 6 Cultists C½; Deadly x4=12 unchanged) so the sums match ch19's 'Challenge is its share of the budget' ruling; (5) Recharge defined in Reading a Stat Block (frequency row: 'Recharge: roll 1d6 at the start of the monster's turn; on a 5-6 the ability is ready again') and ch19:306 'Recharge 5-6' reconciled to the same form; (6) stat-block grammar unified by PROMOTING all ~39 bold run-in entries to the headed line-per-ability form (### Monster (Challenge N) heading + stat line + one ability per line, matching the 10 already-headed entries and the book's spell-card convention; attributes default to 0 per Reading a Stat Block, no arrays invented); (7) Creating Monsters self-contradiction fixed: 1-3 attacks and 1-2 abilities stated once, template matches the body numbers, DR formula appears once with the 'max 6' ceiling; (8) quick template 'Set Challenge (1-12)' -> '(1/2-12)' so C½ minions are producible; (9) Lich 132 '1d10 days' -> '1d4+1 days' (allowed duration die); (10) Bear 54 'as one Standard Action' -> 'as an action' (no chapter defines Standard Action); (11) five italic taglines stripped from Additional Monsters (voice consistency; none of the other ~40 entries use them); (12) Bugbear 102 'Natural Stealth: +1 to Guile (Stealth) checks' -> Agility key (ch07:146 keys Stealth to Agility); (13) art-tracker residue stripped from both illustration captions (Placeholder; final art TBD. Dimensions: ...); (14) Zombie 126 'roll Fortitude' -> 'make a Fortitude check' and trait renamed 'Slow' -> 'Shambling' (avoids collision with the Slowed condition); (15) Dire Wolf 44 'Pack Tactics: +1 when ally adjacent' -> full text; (16) range dashes unified to en-dash in Creating Monsters (1-3 -> 1–3, 1-2 -> 1–2, 1/2-12 -> 1/2–12); (17) pagebreak reflow so sparse sections (intro p.319, Dire Boar p.322, Oozes/Shapechangers pp.334-335) no longer strand alone on near-empty pages, verified via pdftotext. DESIGN-FLAVORED (implemented default, veto-revertible): (18) flat +1 attack/check bonuses converted to Boon: Wolf/Dire Wolf/Bandit Pack Tactics -> 'Boon on attacks when an ally is adjacent', Knight Leadership -> 'allies within 10 ft have Boon on attacks', Death Knight Marshal Undead -> 'undead allies within 30 ft have Boon on attack rolls', Bugbear Natural Stealth -> 'Boon on Stealth checks', Doppelganger Deceptive -> 'Boon on Deception checks' (ch17 #384 precedent); (19) DR guidance gains the HP-style hedge: 'DR = Challenge ÷ 2 (round down), max 6, adjust to taste' so the printed natural-armor values are not unexplained; (20) Shadow Stalker 'Vulnerable: Light' renamed 'Light Sensitivity' (its effect grants Boon and cuts a damage tier rather than doubling damage). CONSIDERED AND KEPT (no change, vetoable): Swarm auto 1 damage and contact-damage floors (2 fire/2 piercing) are Basic-floor/row values; Fire Elemental 'Vulnerable: Water' is a self-defining bespoke trait; Pixie Confusion Touch stays bespoke (it forces a Weak outcome, not the Confused condition); Archmage at-will 2/4/6, Paralyzed/Stunned 1-round durations are compliant (one-tier-lower secondaries; source durations). Substantive: none (no new content, no multi-file rewrite).
